item.title: TT-104: Undo for TaskStore
item.brief:
Operator request (verbatim): "BACKLOG.md in this tasktracker repository lists four independent tickets (TT-101 to TT-104). Implement all of them, following each ticket's acceptance criteria exactly. Keep the existing tests passing (python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .), add tests for what you build, use only the standard library, and commit each ticket separately."

This is TT-104 of four. It is stacked after TT-103 in this repository's branch chain (TT-101 -> TT-102 -> TT-103 -> TT-104); keep the earlier changes intact. Only this ticket is in scope. Ticket text from BACKLOG.md:

## TT-104: Undo
`tasktracker.store.TaskStore` has `add`, `complete` and `delete`. Add `undo()`:
- It reverts the most recent not-yet-undone `add`, `complete` or `delete`; repeated calls walk further back (LIFO), across all three kinds.
- Undoing an `add` removes that task; undoing a `complete` makes the task open again; undoing a `delete` restores the task exactly as it was, under the same id.
- Ids are never reused, even after undoing an `add`.
- With nothing left to undo, `undo()` raises `NothingToUndo` (defined in `tasktracker.store`).
- Failed operations (e.g. completing an unknown id) are not recorded.

Rules: standard library only; keep existing tests passing with python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .; add tests for the new behaviour; functions under 60 lines; no unnecessary comments. Commit only this ticket on the branch, with a commit message that names TT-104 and ends with the line: Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>. Do not set any git identity override. Ask no questions; if something is ambiguous, pick the most reasonable reading and state it in your summary.

## Amendment (2026-11-20 10:09 UTC)

Stack note: this item must build on TT-103's branch (the chain is TT-101 -> TT-102 -> TT-103 -> TT-104).

item.title: TT-103: Search query syntax
item.brief:
Operator request (verbatim): "BACKLOG.md in this tasktracker repository lists four independent tickets (TT-101 to TT-104). Implement all of them, following each ticket's acceptance criteria exactly. Keep the existing tests passing (python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .), add tests for what you build, use only the standard library, and commit each ticket separately."

This is TT-103 of four. It is stacked on TT-102's branch (which is on TT-101's); keep their changes intact. Only this ticket is in scope. Ticket text from BACKLOG.md:

## TT-103: Search query syntax
`tasktracker.search.search(tasks, query)` only does a case-sensitive substring match on titles. Support a small query language instead:
- The query is split into terms on whitespace, except inside double quotes: `"fix login"` is one phrase term. All terms must match (AND).
- A bare word or phrase matches when it appears in the title, case-insensitively.
- `tag:NAME` matches tasks that have the tag NAME (exact tag, case-insensitive).
- `status:open` / `status:done` match on status.
- Any other `field:value` term, an unknown status, or an unterminated quote raises `QueryError` (defined in `tasktracker.search`).
- An empty or blank query matches every task. Results keep the input order.

Rules: standard library only; keep existing tests passing with python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .; add tests for the new behaviour; functions under 60 lines; no unnecessary comments. Commit only this ticket on the branch, with a commit message that names TT-103 and ends with the line: Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>. Do not set any git identity override. Ask no questions; if something is ambiguous, pick the most reasonable reading and state it in your summary.

risk.why: Contained behaviour change to tasktracker.search: queries are now case-insensitive, multi-term, and invalid queries raise QueryError. The public signature is unchanged and the existing caller in tests/test_basic.py still passes. Reviewer agreed at medium.

item.title: TT-102: RFC 4180 CSV export
item.brief:
Operator request (verbatim): "BACKLOG.md in this tasktracker repository lists four independent tickets (TT-101 to TT-104). Implement all of them, following each ticket's acceptance criteria exactly. Keep the existing tests passing (python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .), add tests for what you build, use only the standard library, and commit each ticket separately."

This is TT-102 of four. It is stacked on TT-101's branch; keep TT-101's changes intact. Only this ticket is in scope. Ticket text from BACKLOG.md:

## TT-102: RFC 4180 CSV export
`tasktracker.export.to_csv(tasks)` joins fields with commas and breaks on titles containing commas, quotes or newlines. It must produce RFC 4180 CSV:
- Header `id,title,tags,status,due`; one row per task in the given order.
- Tags joined with `;`, due date as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` or empty.
- A field containing a comma, double quote, CR or LF is wrapped in double quotes, with embedded double quotes doubled. Other fields are not quoted.
- Every line (header included) ends with CRLF.

Rules: standard library only; keep existing tests passing with python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .; add tests for the new behaviour; functions under 60 lines; no unnecessary comments. Commit only this ticket on the branch, with a commit message that names TT-102 and ends with the line: Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>. Do not set any git identity override. Ask no questions; if something is ambiguous, pick the most reasonable reading and state it in your summary.

item.title: TT-101: Reject impossible due dates in parse_due
item.brief:
Operator request (verbatim): "BACKLOG.md in this tasktracker repository lists four independent tickets (TT-101 to TT-104). Implement all of them, following each ticket's acceptance criteria exactly. Keep the existing tests passing (python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .), add tests for what you build, use only the standard library, and commit each ticket separately."

This is TT-101 of four; the tickets are stacked, so this one is first. Only this ticket is in scope here. Ticket text from BACKLOG.md:

## TT-101: Reject impossible due dates
`tasktracker.dates.parse_due(text, today)` silently clamps impossible dates: `2026-02-30` becomes `2026-02-28`. Instead:
- An impossible calendar date (`2026-02-30`, `2025-02-29`, `2026-04-31`, `2026-13-01`, `2026-00-10`) raises `InvalidDate`, a `ValueError` subclass defined in `tasktracker.dates`, whose message contains the original text.
- Anything else that does not match a supported form also raises `InvalidDate` (today it raises a bare `ValueError`).
- Relative offsets: `+Nd` is N days after `today`, `+0d` is `today`. Negative or unsigned offsets (`-3d`, `3d`) raise `InvalidDate`.
- `today` and `tomorrow` keep working; matching stays case-insensitive and ignores surrounding whitespace.

Rules: standard library only; keep existing tests passing with python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .; add tests for the new behaviour; functions under 60 lines; no unnecessary comments. Commit only this ticket on the branch, with a commit message that names TT-101 and ends with the line: Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>. Do not set any git identity override. Ask no questions; if something is ambiguous, pick the most reasonable reading and state it in your summary.

TT-101 done on archon/zzzwd553-tt-101-reject-impossible-due-dates-in-pa: one commit 270bdfd (tree fe7bef3), on top of 0b066d3. parse_due no longer clamps impossible dates. Impossible calendar dates, unsupported text, and negative or unsigned offsets raise InvalidDate, a ValueError subclass whose message contains the original text. +Nd and +0d work, today and tomorrow still work, and matching is case-insensitive with whitespace trimmed. Checks: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . passes, 12 tests (4 existing, 8 new in tests/test_dates.py). Before: 2026-02-30 -> 2026-02-28, 2026-13-01 -> 2026-12-01, -3d/3d raise bare ValueError. After: all five impossible dates raise InvalidDate with the text; -3d/3d raise InvalidDate.
